subject: Grading-honesty sweep: code-house Armory (~20 modules) + dark-arts Linux labs (~5)
description:
Extend the LM-1/#79 grading-honesty methodology to LinuxTerminal-based labs outside linux-mastery. Discovered 2026-07-11 (task #72 hunt): of 131 such labs, 26 call completeTask/completeChallenge with NO lt-error/ok guard. Armory (arm-bash-01..10, arm-sql-01..10) gates purely on cmdLine.includes() command-text, not success — e.g. arm-bash-01:514 `chmod +x` completes even against a nonexistent file (same class as lm-39). Also check 5 dark-arts da-linux-* labs (log-analysis, compromised-server, hidden-files, permission-analysis) for command-regex looseness. NUANCE: apply LM-1 practice-intent judgment per module (beginner intro modules may gate on command-shape intentionally; LM-1 excluded lm-53 tour, flagged lm-20/34). APPROACH: reuse LM-1 task-shape catalog + `ok = !output.includes('lt-error')` + puppeteer honesty probes + per-file harness (see _tools/ai900-ch01-honest-button-test.js). Nancy per file-family, Chris, deploy per-file. Detail in marathon backlog + scratchpad/task72-dishonest-buttons.md. Needs per-module ok-wiring (modules don't currently compute ok).
[2026-07-24 06:23] AUDIT COMPLETE 2026-07-24 (read-only, exhaustive ~215 files). RESULT: dishonest-completion defect concentrated ENTIRELY in Armory = 150 P1 files, 3 families: JS(10) complete-on-load; C(10) click-chips; scroll-credit(130, 12 langs + python-graphics). Logged BUG-021. Dark-arts labs (43) all HONEST (real command/objective engines). Gold-standard fix pattern already in-tree: armory/bash (LinuxTerminal cmd-gate + error-guard) + armory/sql (SQLEngine query-gate). NEEDS operator approach green-light (150-file product-surface rework = architecture per CLAUDE.md 'discuss architecture first'). Recommended: pilot 10 JS + 10 C (indefensible under any pattern) w/ honest checkpoint pattern -> Nancy+Chris gate template -> roll 130 scroll modules. P3 hygiene: sql keyword-match no error-guard; challenge-runner regex-token grading; lab complete-buttons don't re-check state; single-array linux labs skip-to-complete at reduced score.

WITH NANCY: go (clean, ids match hub), cpp (fixed 2 leaks + dead-tracker id mismatch cpp-06/08 -> hub filename-stem ids; 1 'move' keyword flag for Nancy). BUILDING: ruby, php. NEW QC checks banked into TEMPLATE-SPEC from this wave: (1) HUB-ID MATCH (module write-id must == <lang>/index.html MODULES id / filename stem, else dead-tracker - go builder got it right, cpp builder preserved truncated ids, hub decided); (2) COUNT-MATCH sub-check (Nancy: answer magnitude must not coincidentally equal a printed related result's count).
[2026-07-31 13:06] MEASURED 2026-07-31 (ticket's 2026-07-11 figures are stale: it said 26 of 131). Two of my own measurement errors first: (a) my detector only matched 'ok &&' so correctly-guarded lines like 'if (cmd==="id" && ok)' were flagged as violations -- fixing it cut the platform count 432 -> 322 lines; (b) my first glob used *.lab.html and returned ZERO Armory files because they are .module.html -- I nearly reported 'Armory is clean' from a pattern that could not match it.
CURRENT STATE: Armory bash 19 ungated of 44 calls. arm-bash-01 HAS been fixed since the ticket (sets ok, gates 4 of 5) but L521 was MISSED -- the run-the-script task still completes on command text. Armory SQL: all 10 modules entirely ungated, 46 of 46. Dark-arts linux: 10 labs (not the 5 named), 72 calls, ALL ungated, many bare completeTask('x') with no condition at all.
KEY TECHNICAL FINDING: the SQL modules DO execute real queries (SQLEngine runs them against an in-memory DB with genuine failure paths), but SQLEngine._renderError emits '<span style=color:#f87171>Error: ...' -- an INLINE STYLE, not the lt-error CLASS -- and LinuxTerminal has zero SQL knowledge (grep sqlite/SELECT = 0). So the platform's standard guard !output.includes('lt-error') is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to SQL errors. That is almost certainly why all 10 are ungated: the pattern does not work there. Proposed fix is one component change (SQLEngine._renderError emits class=lt-error) rather than a second stringly-typed convention duplicated 10x. Nancy dispatched to rule per family, including which are legitimately practice-intent (arm-sql-01-intro teaching SELECT sqlite_version() may WANT to credit the attempt; arm-sql-09-security crediting lower.includes('union') is clearly wrong). NOTHING CHANGED YET.
[2026-07-31 13:11] CORRECTION 2026-07-31 -- Nancy BLOCKED my plan and was right on all three points. My proposal was, in effect: duplicate held work, reverse documented decisions, and mischaracterise a family.
1. THE FIX I PROPOSED ALREADY EXISTS. Branch armsql-honesty-wip commit a6c03695e (2026-07-22), titled 'HELD, DO NOT DEPLOY', contains the exact _renderError class fix PLUS five real SQLEngine bugs (quoted-INSERT parsing, 0-row UPDATE/DELETE rendering success, GRANT/REVOKE never dispatched, MIN/MAX on TEXT, missing seed). Nancy verified the mechanism TWICE. It is held for a reason my proposal never mentioned: 11 of 12 arm-sql worked-example boxes print FABRICATED output (2026 dates, COUNT=847) contradicting the real 12-row 2024 seed -- a content rebuild, not a gate patch. There is a dedicated status doc at _docs/operations/armsql-honesty-wip-status.md and the whole position is in BUG_TRACKER.md:1216. I searched the CODE but never searched the TRACKER or the BRANCHES for prior decisions on these exact files.
2. arm-bash-01:521 IS NOT A MISS. Three comment lines directly above it read: 'NOTE (BUG-008 pinned): the engine does not execute a created script, so ./hello.sh errors -- gating this on ok would make the task unreachable.' Same at arm-bash-09:339 (sha256sum/md5sum unimplemented) and arm-bash-03:320 (the task TEACHES triggering stderr, so an lt-error is the CORRECT outcome). I flagged the line and did not read the three lines above it. Gating them would manufacture exactly the false-FAIL I had myself called worse than the current false-PASS. arm-bash-04/05/06/10 are likewise PINNED pending a C1(engine-build)-vs-C2(module-rewrite) architecture decision.
3. COUNTS WRONG AGAIN (third detector error today). Armory bash is 45 call sites / 20 ungated, not 44/19 -- my line-based counter missed a line holding two calls; Nancy's number is correct. And dark-arts linux has 23 labs, not 10: the other 13 (nmap-drill, hashcat, hydra, metasploit, privesc, recon-drill, ...) contain ZERO completeTask/completeChallenge and use a different pattern ('advance'), so my detector could not see them. Identical class to my earlier .lab.html-vs-.module.html glob miss, one layer deeper.
RE-SCOPED per Nancy: arm-sql = BLOCK (reconcile the held branch first; content rebuild gates it). arm-bash = BLOCK on the plan as written (pins are decisions, not misses). dark-arts = EXPLORE, and the real population is 23 with 13 never audited. This is not one 137-path problem; it is at minimum four independently-gated decisions.
[2026-07-31 13:23] DARK-ARTS EXPLORE COMPLETE 2026-07-31 -- Nancy's one unblocked slice. Opened and audited all 13 previously-unaudited da-linux labs (the ones my earlier detector returned ZERO for because they use a different completion mechanism).
RESULT: all 13 are HONESTLY GATED. Mechanism is per-task validators -- handleCommand runs task.validate(cmd); on failure it prints an lt-error and does NOT mark the task, on success it marks 'correct'. Every one of the 13 gates its success branch on correct === TASKS.length, so a SKIPPED task never counts toward passing. And none of the 13 calls ModuleProgress at all, so none can grant false module credit. The tracker's 'most already outcome-gated' (2026-07-21) is confirmed, and is actually stronger than stated.
ONE COSMETIC INCONSISTENCY, not a credit defect: updateProgress() computes percent from Object.keys(state.results).length, which counts 'skipped' alongside 'correct', so the progress BAR can read 100% while the correct-count reads low -- and a timer expiry marks all remaining tasks 'skipped', filling the bar. The numeric completedCount and the final success branch both use correct-only, so nothing is falsely credited. Worth tidying, not a defect.
MY DETECTOR WAS FLAWED AGAIN (5th today, harmless direction): I scored validator 'strictness' by counting && occurrences, which penalises the strictest form -- validate: c => c === 'msfconsole' is an EXACT match and scored 0, and c.includes('show options') || c === 'options' accepts two valid spellings of one command and scored as loose. The validators are appropriate; my proxy was not. da-linux-hash-drill has 0 validators because it is a hash-IDENTIFICATION drill (not command-driven) and still gates on correct-only.
NET: dark-arts family needs NO change. #103's remaining scope is arm-sql (blocked behind the held branch + content rebuild) and arm-bash (pins are decisions, plus the 04/05/06/10 architecture call).
